cases.text: We introduce Doppler Correspondence, a geometrically and kinematically derived range-and-Doppler relation for associating consecutive 4D radar and LiDAR scans. Under a short-scan motion approximation, corresponding points have approximately equal scalar scores, each computed from its own range and radial velocity. Doppler therefore guides association before rigid registration, reducing reliance on repetitive geometry without replacing spatial constraints. A lightweight non-iterative algorithm finds matches once in score space, rejects candidates using spatial and score thresholds, and estimates a rigid transformation. Experiments cover sparse and semi-dense radar and dense LiDAR. On Campus2, transformation estimation excluding preprocessing takes 0.16 ms/frame versus 5.9 ms for unseeded point-to-point ICP. Sharp turns can invalidate the approximation and cause drift. An iterative extension, Doppler 4D-ICP, combines fixed Doppler-derived correspondences with repeatedly updated geometric matches.
cases.note: Prioritizes Doppler-guided association, the single-pass baseline, and the distinct iterative extension; retains preprocessing scope and rotation-related failure.

cases.text: V-HOP is a model-based visuo-haptic tracker for 6D object pose during manipulation. It represents heterogeneous tactile inputs and gripper posture as a contact-labeled gripper point cloud, paired with an object CAD cloud positioned by the previous pose estimate. This shared geometry compares the hypothesized object with observed haptic geometry to learn a pose correction across sensor layouts and embodiments. A frozen FoundationPose RGB-D encoder and trainable haptic encoder feed fine-tuned transformers, adapting feature fusion to contact and visibility: vision supports tracking without contact, while haptics supports tracking under severe occlusion. Training uses only synthetic data spanning eight grippers and thirteen objects. On FeelSight-Occlusion, with an unseen hand, tactile sensor type, and object, V-HOP achieves 1.46 mm ADD-S error at 32 FPS, compared with NeuralFeels' 2.14 mm at 3 FPS. NeuralFeels receives ground-truth segmentation; V-HOP does not. Real robot experiments also evaluate tracking and manipulation.
cases.note: Preserves both the hypothesis-versus-observation representation and adaptive feature fusion, with synthetic training scope and the segmentation difference accompanying the benchmark comparison.
